title: His asylum claim was refused and the letter ordered him to leave the country, so he
subtitle: 9 operations from 4 reading(s), pooled. An operation is a NODE: two readings touch only where they put the SAME model's words on a relation. Only models placed in `operations` are here -- `unassigned` carries no words and `reversed` is excluded, so between 18% and 98% of what was sent reaches this graph depending on the rater.

nodes.label: flight to appeal
nodes.statement: Alignment relocates the subject's response from an act of physical self-removal to an act of formal institutional appeal.

nodes.label: action to stance
nodes.statement: Alignment replaces a concrete action verb describing what the subject did with a copula or modal verb describing what is, was, or could be true of him.

nodes.label: erase the trail
nodes.statement: Alignment completes the sentence not with departure itself but with the subject destroying or concealing evidence of it.

nodes.label: departure recedes into procedure
nodes.statement: Under the second condition, verbs naming a concrete physical departure lose rank while verbs naming legal-institutional recourse or bare modal/auxiliary hedging gain rank, so the completion shifts from what someone did toward what they are permitted, obliged, or entitled to do.

nodes.label: dramatic flight turns routine
nodes.statement: Within the single field of leaving, a dramatic or covert verb of flight loses rank while an unmarked, routine verb of travel gains rank, so the completion still narrates departure but in a less charged register.

nodes.label: departure turns to destruction
nodes.statement: Verbs of leaving or plain narration lose rank while verbs naming a violent or destructive act gain rank, so the completion turns from leaving the scene toward harming or destroying something.

nodes.label: Escape Yields to Hedging
nodes.statement: Concrete verbs of physical departure lose ground while modal, auxiliary, and formal-petition verbs gain ground, as if a story of leaving were rewritten into a story of deliberating, being unable, or seeking permission.

nodes.id: OP[x1b.n50.r1] Flight Gives Way to Concealment
nodes.label: Flight Gives Way to Concealment
nodes.statement: Verbs of open, visible departure lose ground to verbs of hiding, destroying, or disposing of belongings and evidence, as if the same story were rewritten from leaving openly to covering one's tracks first.

nodes.label: flight recedes into appeal
nodes.statement: Words naming the subject's own unilateral departure or escape lose rank while words naming a formal appeal or petition directed at an authority gain rank.
